identification.title: He Will Hold Me Fast
identification.artist: Keith & Kristyn Getty (text by Ada R. Habershon, revised with new music by Matt Merker)
identification.notes: Two versions exist. The original is a hymn by Ada R. Habershon (1861-1918), a Plymouth Brethren writer who worked with the Torrey-Alexander campaign, with an early tune by Robert Harkness, introduced at the 1907 Moody Bible Conference at Northfield. The version churches now know is the modern setting: Matt Merker revised the first two stanzas, wrote a third stanza and a new tune, and Keith & Kristyn Getty recorded it on Facing a Task Unfinished and the Together for the Gospel Live III album (2016). The Getty setting is copyrighted (Getty Music; sources give 2013 and 2016 for the date), so it is not public domain, though Habershon's original is. Sources disagree on the exact dates and I found no single account of the arrangement's timeline; CCLI number not confirmed. The list's artist guess of the Gettys is right for the recording churches know. Reviewed as the Merker/Getty setting.

claims.structuralNotes: Three stanzas, a refrain and a repeated closing line in the final sung chorus. Stanza 1 admits the singer's faith may fail, the tempter presses and his love is cold, and answers that Christ must hold him. Stanza 2 says those he saves are his delight and precious to him, that he will not lose them, that his promises last, and that they were bought at great cost. Stanza 3 says Christ bled and died for the singer's life, justice was satisfied, the believer is raised with him to endless life, and he holds on until faith becomes sight at his coming. The refrain grounds all of it in the Savior's love. The voice is first person singular, but each claim is credal: what Christ does, did and will do. The singer's weakness is the foil, not the subject. Christ is named.

claims.claim: The believer's faith and love are weak and temptation is real, but Christ holds him and must hold him.
claims.subject: Perseverance

claims.claim: Those Christ saves are his delight and precious to him, and he will not let their souls be lost.
claims.subject: Assurance and God's delight

claims.claim: Christ's promises last, and believers were bought at a great cost.
claims.subject: Redemption and promise

claims.claim: Christ bled and died for the singer, and justice has been satisfied.
claims.subject: Atonement

claims.claim: The believer is raised with Christ to endless life and is kept until faith becomes sight at his coming.
claims.subject: Resurrection and final perseverance

claims.claim: Christ holds the believer fast because the Savior loves him.
claims.subject: Assurance

strengths.title: Security rests on Christ's keeping
strengths.explanation: The singer admits his weak faith and cold love and answers with Christ's hold on him. Assurance rests on Christ's keeping and love, not on the singer's performance.
strengths.scriptureRationale: No one can snatch Christ's sheep from his hand - the security the refrain sings.

strengths.title: Justice satisfied and the life bought
strengths.explanation: Stanzas 2 and 3 say believers were bought at great cost, that Christ bled and died for the singer, and that justice has been satisfied. Confidence is placed in the cross, not in feeling.
strengths.scriptureRationale: God satisfying justice in Christ's blood - what the third stanza says.

strengths.title: Saved people are God's delight
strengths.explanation: Stanza 2 says those he saves are precious to him, so assurance rests on his regard for them and the promises he keeps, not on their grip.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Christ's sheep held securely in his hand.

strengths.title: Raised with Christ and kept until sight
strengths.explanation: The last stanza names being raised with Christ to endless life and looks to his coming, so assurance becomes a promise of arrival.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Raised with Christ and appearing with him in glory.

theological.assessment: No concern. A clear statement of assurance: weakness admitted, Christ's love and hold as the ground. It reaches the cross, justice satisfied, resurrection life and Christ's coming. Those who hold that salvation can be lost may read the refrain differently, but that is a position faithful Christians dispute, not an error in the song. The Spirit and the church are not named.

strengths.title: A tune a congregation can learn
strengths.explanation: The refrain is easy to catch and returns the room to one line of assurance, so a congregation can join on first hearing.

strengths.title: For the doubting and the suffering
strengths.explanation: It gives a congregation words for weakness and for trust, so it suits funerals, communion and hard seasons.

communal.vocalRangeNote: The Getty setting is commonly led in lower-mid keys such as D or Eb; verify against the chart used. The melody is moderate in range and suits mixed congregations.

range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: The refrain returns to the central confession after each stanza's particular comfort, and the closing chorus repeats it; this deepens rather than fills.
communal.assessment: Congregational and calm. Each singer says 'I' but the content is what Christ does and has done, so the room confesses it together. Three short stanzas can be sung in full.

strengths.title: Christ and his keeping are plain
strengths.explanation: The song says who holds the believer and why, so a visitor hears the promise clearly.

clarity.assessment: Clear. The 'I' of weakness and the 'he' of keeping are never confused, and the doctrine is stated in plain terms.

synthesis.summary: Ada Habershon's 1907 hymn on assurance as heard in Matt Merker's revision and tune, recorded by Keith and Kristyn Getty. The singer's weakness is admitted and Christ's love and hold are the ground: the saved are his delight, bought at cost, justice satisfied, raised with Christ and kept until he comes. No concern was found; the Spirit and church are not named. Copyrighted Merker/Getty setting.

scriptureReferences.relevance: Christ's sheep held in his hand - the security of the refrain.
Justice satisfied in Christ's blood - the third stanza.
Raised with Christ and appearing with him in glory.
God completing what he began - the hope of arrival.
